answers.explanation: Special-purpose processors don't run user programs. It's still a single-processor system.
Tightly coupled: they share the bus, and often the clock, memory, and devices.
Keeping parts working together costs time, and processors compete for memory.
Sharing one disk beats copying the data to many machines.
Service continues in proportion to the surviving hardware.
It goes beyond graceful degradation, and needs duplicated hardware plus failure detection.
Throughput is work completed per unit of time.
Multicore chips put several processors in every device.
